From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Threshold note on the Seller's preamble.** The "market context" and the statements that positions were "settled at principal level" and are "FINAL / not to be re-opened" are the other side's advocacy, not instructions to us. Nothing in our instructions records any principal-level agreement on these points. Treat every "FINAL" marker as open and ask the deal team to confirm whether Wattlebridge principals actually agreed anything. Note also the Disclosure Letter is internally candid in ways the Seller Update is not (e.g. no Bluefen consent, Riverlark not repaid, bonuses missing from funds flow) – the Disclosure Letter undercuts the Seller Update on several points, and we should use that.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims.
- Buyer wants: Materially higher cap for general warranties (target 50–100% of price; fall-back 30–40%), with Tax, IP and the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) sitting outside this cap.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 100% of price, settle no lower than ~30–35%, with carve-outs.** Reason: the known issues (Bluefen 30% revenue, Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses, privacy incident) show real exposure that a 20% cap could swallow with one claim.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 (≈1.04%) operating as a deductible (excess only).
- Buyer wants: Lower de minimis (AUD 5,000–10,000), basket at ≤0.5–1% operating as a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded), and no thresholds for Tax, Title/Fundamental or specific indemnity claims.
- Recommendation: **Counter: de minimis AUD 10,000, basket AUD 120,000–240,000 tipping, with related claims aggregated.** Reason: an excess-only basket plus a high de minimis silently gives away up to AUD 250k on every loss and lets related small breaches escape.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months for general warranties, and a default that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (two audit cycles); 7 years (or statutory period + 6 months) for Tax; indefinite or 6+ years for Title/Fundamental; indemnities to run per their own terms.
- Recommendation: **Counter at 24 months and strike the "applies to all Claims" default.** Reason: 18 months barely covers one post-Completion audit, and the catch-all default would drag Tax, Title and indemnity claims into the short period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of price, no de minimis/basket, 6+ years (or indefinite).
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Reason: "administrative simplicity" is not a reason for a buyer to accept a 20% cap on getting the shares it paid AUD 24m for.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: silent – and Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 say limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature", which on its face would purport to limit fraud.
- Buyer wants: Express carve-out that no cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause applies to fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- Recommendation: **Insert express fraud carve-out; non-negotiable.** Reason: an attempt to limit liability for fraud is unenforceable in NSW in any event, but its presence signals intent and will be litigated – remove the ambiguity.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and all public records; para 1.4 reserves that nothing is an admission of anything.
- Buyer wants: Only "fairly disclosed" matters count (disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter); specific disclosures against specific warranties; no disclosure of public registers beyond ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches at a dated snapshot; data room as a locked, indexed USB/exhibit; no "bring-down" of general disclosure at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject general disclosure; require fair-disclosure standard and a frozen data room index.** Reason: blanket disclosure of a data room plus "publicly searchable records" effectively reverses the warranty package and shifts all diligence risk to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: Delete. At most, a narrow qualifier limited to *actual* knowledge of a named small group of Buyer individuals of a matter that is a breach, with no constructive/imputed knowledge and no adviser knowledge.
- Recommendation: **Delete; fall-back to actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals only.** Reason: "discoverable" is constructive knowledge and, combined with SPA-N-006, would eliminate nearly every warranty claim.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: "reasonable endeavours"; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter admits no final consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: Unconditional written Bluefen consent under clause 11.2, with the 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived, as a Condition Precedent in the Buyer's sole discretion to waive; Seller "all reasonable endeavours/best endeavours"; no Seller ability to satisfy the CP by delivering a conditional consent; specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates within 12 months of Completion.
- Recommendation: **Make it a hard CP (unconditional consent + conditions satisfied) with a 12-month revenue-loss protection.** Reason: Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m), and the Seller's own letter confirms consent is not in hand.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter confirms AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge, and clause 8.1 change-of-control.
- Buyer wants: Repayment from Seller's proceeds via the funds flow at Completion, executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion as Completion deliverables; Riverlark change-of-control consent/waiver obtained; any amount not discharged treated as Debt in the cash-free/debt-free price adjustment.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-Completion release; require payout and discharge at Completion, deducted from price.** Reason: the deal is debt-free/cash-free – the Buyer must not inherit AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a change-of-control default on a promise of a later release.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter admits they are triggered by Completion and silent on super/payroll tax/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and all on-costs (realistically AUD 480k–500k+) treated as Transaction Costs/Debt in the completion accounts or deducted from the price; paid through Company payroll pre-Completion funded by Seller, or specifically indemnified; Seller to confirm no other change-of-control payments.
- Recommendation: **Treat as Debt/Transaction Costs with grossed-up on-costs and a specific indemnity.** Reason: they are Company liabilities crystallising on Completion, so "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the money actually leaves the Seller's pocket.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000) and "adequate". Disclosure Letter confirms IP in SOW3 Project Materials does not transfer until all SOW3 fees are paid, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment exists.
- Buyer wants: Payment of the AUD 180k and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as Completion deliverables; indemnity covering the payment *and* all loss from any failure of title to SOW3 (and prior SOW) materials, including re-development, licence or infringement costs; IP warranty uncapped by the general regime.
- Recommendation: **Make payment + confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable and widen the indemnity to all consequences of defective title.** Reason: the exposure is not AUD 180k, it is ownership of core product IP, which the Seller's own letter says has not yet transferred.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external email, scope and access unknown, notification not assessed.
- Buyer wants: Completion of the investigation (or a defined investigation plan) pre-Completion; written assessment against the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme and any contractual notification obligations (including to Bluefen/Mossvale); specific uncapped-or-separately-capped indemnity for regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation; warranty that no other incidents exist.
- Recommendation: **Specific indemnity plus a pre-Completion investigation/NDB assessment deliverable.** Reason: the Seller cannot both say it is immaterial and admit it does not know whether unauthorised access occurred or notification is required.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter will not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and flags they should be "read together for timing/scope".
- Buyer wants: Confirmation whether the three contracts are one arrangement split to stay under approval thresholds; whether the liability is committed pre-Completion (then Debt/accrued liability) or can be terminated; working-capital target/normalisation to reflect them; covenant prohibiting new commitments >AUD 50k between signing and Completion without Buyer consent.
- Recommendation: **Treat committed amounts as Debt or accrued liability in completion accounts and add a pre-Completion conduct covenant.** Reason: AUD 330k of linked renewals timed around Completion is a leakage question, not a given, until the Seller answers the questions its own letter leaves open.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: one regime – caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; limitation default extends to all Claims.
- Buyer wants: Distinct tiers: (i) General Warranties; (ii) Tax Warranties and Tax Indemnity; (iii) Fundamental/Title; (iv) Specific Indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Bluefen, leakage); (v) fraud – each with its own cap, threshold and period, with specific indemnities and leakage recoverable on a first-dollar basis.
- Recommendation: **Reject the single regime; insert a tiered limitation schedule.** Reason: a single "all Claims" regime converts every known, specific risk into a general-warranty claim subject to a 20% cap and 18-month tail.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register (DD-012); Disclosure Letter notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: Independent verification – ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and Harbourglass, review of constitution and any shareholder agreements/options/convertibles, Riverlark security documents (likely a share mortgage or general security over the shares); Completion deliverables of share transfer, share certificate, board minutes, and resignations; fundamental title warranty uncapped (per SPA-N-004).
- Recommendation: **Run independent title/encumbrance searches now; do not rely on DD-012.** Reason: a self-maintained register is the Seller's assertion, not evidence, and the Riverlark security almost certainly sits over the very shares being sold.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: "settled under the general regime" – i.e. 20% cap, AUD 25k/250k thresholds, 18 months, buyer-knowledge and general disclosure.
- Buyer wants: Separate Tax Indemnity (pre-Completion tax, first-dollar, capped at price, 7 years, no knowledge/disclosure qualification except specific disclosure); Tax Warranties on the same timeline; IP Warranties (ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments, Ironquay chain of title) with a higher cap (50–100%) and 3–5 years; both outside the general basket.
- Recommendation: **Reject; treat Tax and IP as open and negotiate separate regimes.** Reason: tax exposures typically surface after 18 months, and IP ownership is the asset being bought – neither belongs under a 20%/18-month general cap.

---

**Priority order for the mark-up:** (1) Riverlark payout at Completion; (2) tiered limitation regime with fraud carve-out and uncapped Fundamental/Tax; (3) Bluefen as a hard CP; (4) delete general disclosure and buyer-knowledge qualifier; (5) bonuses/Sandbar/Ironquay/DD-006 into funds flow and specific indemnities. Let me know if you want this converted into a clause-by-clause mark-up or an issues list for the principals.
